metadata.title: Minimal mass blow-up solutions for the $L^2$ critical NLS with inverse-square potential

nodes.name: Focusing NLS with inverse-square potential
nodes.statement: In this paper, we initiate the study of finite time blow-up solutions of the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS) with an attractive inverse-square potential, \begin{align} i\partial_t u + \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u &= 0, \quad u(0,\cdot)=u_0\in H^1(\rn), \end{align} in the $L^2$ critical case, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, with $N\ge 3$.
nodes.statement_short: The governing equation: focusing NLS with an attractive $c|x|^{-2}$ potential, studied at the $L^2$ critical power.

nodes.name: Hardy's inequality
nodes.statement: We shall fix the coupling constant $c\in(0,c_*)$, where $c_*=(N-2)^2/4$ is the best constant in Hardy's inequality: \begin{equation} c_*\intrn \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \le \intrn |\nabla u|^2 dx, \quad u\in H^1(\rn). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The sharp Hardy inequality with best constant $c_*=(N-2)^2/4$, fixing the admissible range of the coupling constant.

nodes.name: Conservation of mass
nodes.statement: Along the flow of~\eqref{inls}, we have conservation of the $L^2$ norm, also known as the \emph{mass}: \begin{equation} \Vert u(t)\Vert_{L^2_x} \equiv \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2_x}, \end{equation}

nodes.name: Conservation of energy
nodes.statement: and of the \emph{energy}: \begin{equation} E(u(t))=\frac12 \intrn|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\diff x - \frac{c}{2}\int_{\rn}\frac{|u(t,x)|^2}{|x|^2}dx - \frac{1}{p+1}\intrn|u(t,x)|^{p+1}\diff x \equiv E(u_0). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The conserved energy: kinetic term minus inverse-square potential term minus the nonlinear term.

nodes.name: Two-sided bound on the Hardy functional
nodes.statement: Moreover by Hardy's inequality, for all $c\in (0,c_*]$, \begin{equation} \left(1-\frac{c}{c_*}\right) \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx\le H(u)\le \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $c<c_*$ the Hardy functional $H$ is comparable to $\Vert\nabla u\Vert_{L^2}^2$, hence an equivalent seminorm.

nodes.name: Stationary elliptic equation for standing waves
nodes.statement: Indeed, $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$ is a (global) solution of~\eqref{inls} if and only if $\ffi\in H^1(\rn)$ solves the nonlinear elliptic equation \begin{equation} \Delta\ffi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\ffi - \ffi + |\ffi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\ffi=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Standing waves $e^{it}\varphi$ solve the NLS exactly when $\varphi$ solves this stationary elliptic equation.

nodes.name: Positivity of the energy below the ground-state mass
nodes.statement: The proof of this theorem relies on the inequality \begin{equation} E(u)\ge \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\rn), \end{equation} which follows from a sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality established in Section~\ref{global.sec}.
nodes.statement_short: Below the ground-state mass the energy controls the Hardy functional from below.

nodes.name: A priori bound on the Hardy functional
nodes.statement: Namely, we have \begin{equation} H(u(t)) \le 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1}, \end{equation} which implies global existence.
nodes.statement_short: Conservation of mass and energy turns the previous inequality into a uniform-in-time bound on $H(u(t))$.

nodes.name: Energy of a phase modulation
nodes.statement_short: Expansion of the energy under the phase modulation $u\mapsto ue^{is\theta}$, quadratic in $s$.

nodes.name: Hardy functional
nodes.statement: For our analysis it is convenient to introduce the {\em Hardy functional}, defined on $H^1(\rn)$ by \[ H(u)=\int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx -c\int_{\rn}\frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx. \]

nodes.name: $L^2$ scaling and $L^2$ criticality
nodes.statement: Now, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$ yields $2/(p-1)=N/2$ and, as in the classical case $c=0$, \eqref{inls} is invariant under the {\em $L^2$ scaling} \[ u(t,x) \to u_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2 t, \lambda x) \quad (\lambda>0). \] This transformation preserves the $L^2$ norm and \eqref{inls} is called {\em $L^2$ critical}.
nodes.statement_short: The scaling $u\mapsto\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2t,\lambda x)$ leaves both the equation and the $L^2$ norm invariant, whence $L^2$ criticality.

nodes.name: The natural energy space $\mathcal{H}$
nodes.statement: The natural energy space associated with \eqref{inls}, $\mathcal{H}=\{u\in L^2(\rn) : H(u)<+\infty\}$, then satisfies $H^1(\rn)\subsetneq\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Weinstein functional $J^{p,N}$
nodes.statement: Consider the Weinstein functional \[ J^{p,N}(u):=\frac{H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|u\|^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}_{L^2}}{\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Scaling-invariant quotient whose infimum yields the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant, with $H$ in place of the Dirichlet energy.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Ground states and the minimal mass $M_\mathrm{gs}$
nodes.statement: In the case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, we call {\em ground states} the minimizers of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$ that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}. We denote the set of ground states by $\mathcal{G}$. In view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem}~(b), there exists $M_\mathrm{gs}>0$ such that $\Vert Q\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ for all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$. We call $M_\mathrm{gs}$ the {\em minimal mass}.
nodes.statement_short: Ground states are the positive radial minimizers of the Weinstein functional; they all share the mass $M_\mathrm{gs}$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
differentia: that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}

nodes.name: The space $\Sigma$ and the variance $\Gamma(t)$
nodes.statement: We let \[ \Sigma :=\{u \in H^1(\rn) : xu \in L^2(\rn) \}, \] and for $u(t)\in\Sigma$, we introduce \[ \Gamma(t):=\int_{\rn} |x|^2|u(t,x)|^2dx. \]

nodes.name: The family $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ of minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: Taking into account the above symmetries of~\eqref{inls} we obtain, for each ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, a 3-parameter family $(S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0})_{T\in\R,\lambda_0>0,\gamma_0\in\R}$ of minimal mass solutions of~\eqref{inls} blowing up in finite time, defined as \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit 3-parameter family obtained by pseudo-conformally transforming the standing wave $e^{it}Q$.
nodes.genus: 3-parameter family of minimal mass solutions of~\eqref{inls} blowing up in finite time

nodes.name: Local well-posedness (Theorem 5.1 of [suzuki])
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$. For any initial value $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$, there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$. Moreover, the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$. Finally, if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
nodes.statement_short: $H^1$ local well-posedness for the inverse-square NLS, with the blow-up alternative and global existence in the $L^2$ subcritical range.
conclusions: there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$
the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$
if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global

nodes.name: Sharp global well-posedness below the ground-state mass
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$. If $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}, \end {equation} then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
nodes.statement_short: Every $H^1$ solution whose mass is strictly below the ground-state mass is global.
conclusions: then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global

nodes.name: Classification of minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$. Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
nodes.statement_short: Every minimal mass finite-time blow-up solution equals, up to symmetries, a pseudo-conformal transform of a ground state.
assumptions: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$
conclusions: Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, $u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)$

nodes.name: Attainment of the Weinstein minimization problem
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$, \[ \alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u) \] is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation \begin{equation} N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0. \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \alpha_{p,N}=2\frac{\|Q\|_{L^2}^{p-1}}{p+1}. \end{equation} In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.statement_short: The infimum of the Weinstein functional is attained by a positive radial solution of the associated Euler--Lagrange equation.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: $\alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u)$ is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation $N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0$
In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.

nodes.name: Sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$ and $u\in H^1(\rn)$, we have \begin{equation} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}, \end{equation} where \[ \alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}} \quad\text{in the critical case} \quad p=1+\frac{4}{N}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Sharp interpolation inequality with the Hardy functional replacing the Dirichlet energy, with best constant given by the minimal mass.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: $\Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}$
$\alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}}$ in the critical case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$

nodes.name: Pseudo-conformal transformation
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}. Then, for all $T\in\R$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2$ critical inverse-square NLS is invariant under the pseudo-conformal transformation, which preserves mass.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
assumptions: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}.
conclusions: the function $u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right)$ is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$

nodes.name: Explicit minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: For all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $T\in\R$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$, the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right), \end{equation} is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$.
nodes.statement_short: The explicit family $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ solves the equation and blows up at the conformal rate $(T-t)^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
conclusions: the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right)$, is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$
which blows up with speed $\Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t}$ as $t\to T$, for some $C>0$

nodes.name: Variational characterization of ground states
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H^1(\rn)$ be such that \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0. \end{equation} Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Any zero-energy function of minimal mass is a phase times a rescaled ground state.
assumptions: Let $v\in H^1(\rn)$ be such that $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(v)=0$.
conclusions: Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$

nodes.name: Compactness of minimal mass sequences
nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $\{v_n\}_{n\in\nat}\subset H^1(\rn)$ satisfying \begin{equation} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}, \quad 0<\limsup_{n\in\N}H(v_n)<+\infty, \quad \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}E(v_n)\le 0. \end{equation} Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in\nat}$, $\gamma_0\in\R$ and $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Minimal mass sequences with asymptotically nonpositive energy converge in $H^1$, up to a subsequence and a phase, to a ground state.
conclusions: Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in\nat}$, $\gamma_0\in\R$ and $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that $\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0$

nodes.name: Virial identities
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} on $[0,T)$, such that $u(t)\in \Sigma$ for all $t\in [0,T)$. Then for all $t\in[0,T)$ the following identities hold: \begin{equation} \Gamma'(t)=4\im\int_{\rn} \overline{u}(t,x)(\nabla u(t,x)\cdot x)dx \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \Gamma''(t)=16E(u)+\frac{4}{p+1}(N-Np+4)\int_{\rn} |u(t,x)|^{p+1}dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: First and second derivatives of the variance $\Gamma$ along the flow; the potential term drops out by homogeneity.
assumptions: Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} on $[0,T)$, such that $u(t)\in \Sigma$ for all $t\in [0,T)$.
conclusions: $\Gamma'(t)=4\im\int_{\rn} \overline{u}(t,x)(\nabla u(t,x)\cdot x)dx$

nodes.name: Banica's Cauchy--Schwarz inequality (Lemma 2.1 in [banica])
nodes.statement_short: At the critical mass, the momentum-type functional is dominated by $\sqrt{2E(u)}$ times a weighted $L^2$ norm.

nodes.name: Phase invariance, Pohozaev identity and equality of masses of minimizers
nodes.statement:
oindent (a) Note that, by phase invariance of $J^{p,N}$, if $u$ is a minimizer so is $e^{i	heta}u, \ 	heta\in\R$. \medskip 
oindent (b) For $p=1+ rac{4}{N}$, the Pohozaev identity for \eqref{sinls} implies that any minimizer $u$ of $J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}$ satisfies $E(u)=0$, that is \[ H(u)= rac{1}{1+ rac{2}{N}}\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}, \] and so  egin{equation} J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}(u) = rac{H(u)\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}} = rac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{1+ rac{2}{N}}. \end{equation} Therefore, all minimizers have the same mass. \medskip 
oindent (c) The proof of Proposition~ef{charact.prop} below shows that all minimizers are positive and radial, up to a global phase factor.
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers are phase-invariant, have zero energy by Pohozaev, hence all share the same mass, and are positive and radial up to a phase.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Behaviour of ground states under the $L^2$ scaling
nodes.statement: The $L^2$ scaling $u_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda{x})$ yields \[ H(u_\lambda)=\lambda^2H(u), \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}, \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}=\lambda^2 \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}, \quad \text{hence} \quad J^{p,N}(u_\lambda)=J^{p,N}(u). \] Therefore, if $Q$ is a ground state, then $Q_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x)$ is again a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, satisfying $\Vert Q_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and the rescaled Euler--Lagrange equation \[ \Delta Q_\lambda+ \frac{c}{|x|^2}Q_\lambda-\lambda^{2} Q_\lambda + |Q_\lambda|^{\frac{4}{N}}Q_\lambda=0. \] It follows from Remark~\ref{minmass.rem} below that the ground states are the solutions of \eqref{sinls} with smallest mass.
nodes.statement_short: Rescaling a ground state gives another minimizer of the same mass, solving the Euler--Lagrange equation with frequency $\lambda^2$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Ground states have minimal mass among solutions of the stationary equation
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} that any solution $\ffi$ of \eqref{sinls} satisfies $\|\ffi\|_{L^2}\ge M_\mathrm{gs}$. Otherwise, applying Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} with $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$, one could construct a finite time blow-up solution below the minimal mass threshold, which would contradict our global well-posedness result, Theorem~\ref{global.thm}.
nodes.statement_short: No solution of the stationary equation can have mass below $M_\mathrm{gs}$, else the pseudo-conformal transform would contradict global well-posedness.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Reduction of the family to the single solution $S$
nodes.statement: Note that the blow-up solutions of the family exhibited in Proposition~\ref{blow-up_sol.prop} can all be retrieved from the solution \[ S(t,x) := S_{0,1,0}(t,x) = e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4t}} e^{-\frac{i}{t}} \frac{1}{|t|^{N/2}}Q\left(-\frac{x}{t}\right), \] defined on $(-\infty,0)$ and which blows up at $t=0$ with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{|t|}\quad \text{as } t\uparrow0, \] for some $C>0$. Indeed, all the solutions $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are equal to $S$, up to the symmetries (a), (b) and (c) stated in the introduction. Namely, if we apply the changes $u(t,x)\to \lambda_0^{-N/2}u(\lambda_0^{-2}t,\lambda_0^{-1}x)$, $u(t,x)\to u(t-T,x)$ and finally $u(t,x)\to e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$ to $S$, we obtain $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$.
nodes.statement_short: The whole 3-parameter blow-up family is the orbit of the single solution $S$ under time translation, phase and scaling.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Virial identity in the $L^2$ critical case
nodes.statement: In the $L^2$ critical case, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, (\ref{virialtwo}) reduces to \begin{equation} \Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: At the critical power the second virial derivative is the constant $16E(u_0)$.

nodes.name: Local well-posedness and compactness at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: However, it is not clear to us that local well-posedness holds in this case. Trachanas and Zographopoulos \cite[Theorem~3.1]{greeks} claim that (in the radial case) it follows by adapting a proof by Cazenave, but we were not able to carry this through. Let us briefly explain why.
nodes.statement_short: Whether the inverse-square NLS is locally well-posed at the critical coupling $c=c_*$ is left open.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the ground state for $c>0$
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, for $c>0$, we are not aware of any uniqueness result for \eqref{sinls} on $\rn$. Uniqueness results for radial solutions of nonlinear elliptic PDEs are typically based on an intricate analysis of the corresponding ODEs in the radial variable $r=|x|$, see {\it e.g.}~\cite{kwong,coffman,peletier,yanagida}. We shall not consider this problem here.
nodes.statement_short: Whether the positive radial solution of the stationary equation is unique when $c>0$ is unknown.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 (attainment of the Weinstein minimization problem)
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*} Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing. Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$. Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$. Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}. Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Direct method of the calculus of variations: Schwarz-symmetrize and rescale a minimizing sequence, extract a weak limit that attains the infimum, then read off the Euler--Lagrange equation.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (sharp global well-posedness)
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded. We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \] Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \] Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Combine conservation of mass and energy with the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality to bound $H(u(t))$, then invoke the blow-up alternative.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 (pseudo-conformal transformation)
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives. For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \] It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: every term of the equation picks up the same conformal prefactor, so the transformed function again solves the equation.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2 (explicit minimal mass blow-up solutions)
nodes.statement: The proposition is a simple consequence of Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} applied to the global solution \[ u_{Q,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\lambda_0^2 t}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x), \] which is given by applying the scaling and phase symmetries to the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{it}Q(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the pseudo-conformal transformation to the scaled, phase-shifted standing wave $e^{it}Q$.

Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~ef{charact.prop}. \medskip

If the above claim is not true, then using a diagonal argument we can construct a subsequence $\{v_{n_{k_l}}\}$, and a sequence of pairwise disjoint annuli \[ A_j=\{x\inn : R_j<|x|<R_j+a_j\} \quad	ext{with}\quad R_{j+1}>R_j+a_j, \] such that, for all $j\in\{1,\dots,l\}$, \[ \int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx\ge  ar \delta:=  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{20}>0 \quad	ext{for all} \ n_{k_l}\in\N. \] But then \[ \intrn|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \ge \sum_{j\in\N}\int_{A_j}|

abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx=+\infty. \] In view of \eqref{hardy2} this contradicts \eqref{a}, and completes the proof of \eqref{e1}. We will now combine \eqref{e1} with the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN} and the assumption on the energy in \eqref{a} to reach a contradiction. Using Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^{p+1}(n)$. Hence, by \eqref{a},  egin{align*} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})\le rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx = rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx, \end{align*} and so, by \eqref{e1},  egin{align} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)< rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx. \end{align} Using again Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we also have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^2(n)$, which implies \[ M_\mathrm{gs}=\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^2} =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|w_k\|_{L^2}. \] Therefore, \eqref{GN} applied to $w_k$ yields \[  rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx \le\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\left( rac{\|w_k\|_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}ight)^{ rac4N}H(w_k) = \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k), \] which, together with \eqref{e4}, leads to the contradiction \[ \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)<\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k). \] This shows that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$ and completes the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. nodes.statement_short: Rule out vanishing and dichotomy in the concentration-compactness trichotomy, prove the translations stay bounded via Hardy plus Gagliardo--Nirenberg, then identify the limit by the variational characterization.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (classification of minimal mass blow-up solutions)
nodes.statement:
Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} such that $\|u\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u) =+\infty$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~1.} Let $\{t_n\}_{n\in
at} \subset eal$ be a sequence of times such that $t_n\uparrow T$ as $nightarrow\infty$. We set \[ u_n=u(t_n), \quad \lambda_n^2=H(u_n), \quad v_n(x)=\lambda_n^{-N/2}u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x). \] We note that $\lambda_nightarrow\infty$ as $nightarrow\infty$, and $\|v_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_0\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ by the $L^2$ scaling. Furthermore, \[  egin{split} H(v_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)=1. \end{split} \] On the other hand, by conservation of the energy, \[  egin{split} E(v_n)&= rac12\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)- rac{1}{p+1}\lambda_n^{-2}\int_{n} |u_n(y)|^{p+1}dy\ &=\lambda_n^{-2} E(u_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}E(u_0)	o 0 \quad 	ext{as} \ n	o\infty. \end{split} \] Hence, by Proposition ef{compact.prop}, there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $\gamma_0\ineal$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that, up to a subsequence,  egin{equation} \lim_{nightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0, \end{equation} where $Q_{\lambda_0}(x)=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2.} We now prove that $u_n$ concentrates all of its mass at $x=0$ as $nightarrow\infty$. We show that, in the sense of distributions, \[ |u_n|^2ightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\delta_0. \] Indeed, for any $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(n)$, using the change of variables $y=\lambda_n^{-1}x$ we find that \[  egin{split} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy &=\int_{n}|u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x)|^2\varphi(\lambda^{-1}_nx)\lambda_n^{-N}dx =\int_{n}|v_n(x)|^2\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx\ &=\int_{n}(|v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2)\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx+\int_{n} |Q(x)|^2\varphi(0)dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2(\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0))dx. \end{split} \] Thus, we obtain \[  egin{split} \Big|\int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy -M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0)\Big| &\le \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty}\int_{n}||v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2|dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2|\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0)|dx. \end{split} \] We conclude this step by noticing that $|v_n|^2$ converges strongly to $|Q|^2$ in $L^1(n)$ from (ef{b}), so the first integral vanishes as $nightarrow\infty$. Since $\lambda_nightarrow\infty$ the second integral also converges to zero by the dominated convergence theorem. Hence, we obtain  egin{equation} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dyightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0). \end{equation} \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~3.} We now show that $u(t)\in\Sigma$ for all $t\in[0,T)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty_0(n)$ be a radial and non-negative function such that $\phi(x)=|x|^2$ for $|x|\le 1$. It is easy to see that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \[ |
abla \phi (x) |^2\le C\phi(x) \] for all $x\inn$. Indeed, since $\phi$ is radially symmetric we may choose $f\in C(eal,eal_+) $, such that $\phi(|x|)=f(|x|)$. By Taylor's formula, for all $r\ineal$ and $h\ineal$ there exists $y\in[r,r+h]$, such that \[ 0\le f(r+h)=f(r)+f'(r)h+ rac{f''(y)}{2}h^2\le f(r)+f'(r)h+C'h^2, \] where $C'=1+\max_{r\ineal} rac{|f'(r)|}{2}>0$. Since the right-hand side is a positive quadratic polynomial, we must have that $|f'(r)|^2-4C'f(r)\le 0$, thus $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$, where $C=4C'>0$. For all $R>0$, we define $\phi_R(x)=R^2\phi(x/R)$, and for all $t\in[0,T)$, \[ \Gamma_R(t)=\int_{n}\phi_R(x)|u(t,x)|^2dx. \] A direct calculation, similar to the proof of Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, yields that \[ \Gamma_R'(t)=2	ext{Re}\int\phi_R ar{u}\partial_tu =-2	ext{Im}\int\phi_R ar{u}(\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u) =2\int
abla\phi_R\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u}
abla u). \] Since $\|u\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$, we can apply Lemma ef{banica.lem} and the inequality $|
abla\phi_R|^2\le C\phi_R$, to get \[ |\Gamma'_R(t)|\le 2\sqrt{2E(u)}\Big(\int|
abla\phi_R|^2|u|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le C\sqrt{E(u_0)}\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}. \] By integrating between a fixed $t\in[0,T)$ and $t_n$, we obtain, \[ |\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}-\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t_n)}|\le C|t-t_n|. \] Applying (ef{c}) in Step 2, we get \[ \Gamma_R(t_n)=\int_{n} |u_n(x)|^2\phi_R(x)dxightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\phi_R(0)=0. \] Thus, letting $n	o\infty$ in the last inequality, we obtain, for all $t\in [0,T)$ and all $R>0$, \[ \Gamma_R(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] Since the right-hand side of the last expression is independent of $R$, letting $R	o\infty$ yields, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)\in\Sigma \quad	ext{and}\quad 0\le \Gamma(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] From this estimate, we can extend by continuity $\Gamma(t)$ at $t=T$ by setting $\Gamma(T)=0$, from which we also obtain $\Gamma'(T)=0$. Moreover, since $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and $u$ is a solution of~\eqref{inls}, we may apply Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, and by (ef{virialthree}) we obtain $\Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0)$, which finally gives, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ \Gamma(t) = 8E(u_0)(T-t)^2. \] Letting $t=0$, we find, using identity (ef{virialone}) \[ \Gamma(0)=\int |x|^2|u_0|^2= 8E(u_0)T^2 \quad 	ext{and}\quad \Gamma'(0)= 4\int x\cdot\im(\overline{u_0}
abla u_0) = -16E(u_0)T. \] \medskip 
oindent {\em Step 4.} We apply identity \eqref{valeria} with $u_0$, $s= rac{1}{2T}$, and $	heta(x)= rac{|x|^2}{2}$ to get \[  egin{split} E(u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}})&=E(u_0)+ rac{1}{2T}\int x\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u_0}
abla u_0) + rac{1}{8T^2}\int|x|^2|u_0|^2\ &=E(u_0)+ rac{1}{2T}(-4E(u_0))+ rac{1}{8T^2}(8E(u_0)T^2)=0. \end{split} \] Note that this calculation justifies, {\em a posteriori}, the application of~\eqref{valeria} with $	heta(x)= rac{|x|^2}{2}
ot\in C_0^{\infty}(n)$. Since $\|u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}})=0$, we can deduce from Proposition ef{charact.prop} that there exist $\lambda_1>0$, $\gamma_1\ineal$, and $\wt{Q}\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ u_0(x)=e^{i\gamma_1}e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\lambda_1^{N/2}\wt{Q}(\lambda_1x). \] Finally, we use the pseudo-conformal transformation. We define $	ilde\lambda_0=\lambda_1T>0$ and $	ilde\gamma_0=\gamma_1-\lambda_1^2T\ineal$, and write $u_0$ as \[ u_0(x)=e^{i	ilde\gamma_0}e^{i rac{	ilde\lambda^2_0}{T}} e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0}{T}\Big)^{N/2}\wt{Q}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0x}{T}\Big). \] Thus, $u_0=S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}(0)$, where $S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}$ is defined by (ef{S2.def}). By invoking uniqueness of the solution of (ef{inls}), we find that $u(t)=S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}(t)$ for all $t\in[0,T)$, which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale along a blow-up sequence and apply the compactness proposition, deduce mass concentration at the origin, use Banica's inequality to get $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and the virial identity to pin down $\Gamma$, then identify $u_0$ by the variational characterization.

nodes.name: Scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Check that the two-parameter dilation-and-amplitude scaling leaves the Weinstein quotient unchanged.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Normalized symmetrized minimizing sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing. Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Replace the minimizing sequence by its Schwarz symmetrization and rescale it so that mass and Hardy functional both equal one.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Weak limit attains the infimum
nodes.statement: In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$. Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Radial compactness plus weak lower semi-continuity force the weak limit to be a minimizer with unit mass and unit Hardy functional.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Euler--Lagrange equation for the minimizer
nodes.statement: Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}.
nodes.statement_short: Write out $DJ^{p,N}=0$ and normalize the minimizer into the stated Euler--Lagrange form, giving the sharp constant.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Rescaling minimizers into solutions of the stationary equation
nodes.statement: Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: In the critical case, fix the frequency by an explicit $L^2$ rescaling to land on the stationary equation.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Reduction via the blow-up alternative
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded. We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Reduce global existence to an a priori bound on $H(u(t))$ and express $H$ through the energy.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Apply the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the nonlinear term by the Hardy functional times the mass ratio to the power $4/N$.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Absorb the nonlinear term using conservation laws
nodes.statement: Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Since the mass ratio is $<1$, the nonlinear term is absorbed and $H(u(t))$ stays bounded by $2E(u_0)$ times a constant.
nodes.section: 2 Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Compute the time derivative and Laplacian of $u_T$
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the conformal ansatz in time and space.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Transform the nonlinear term
nodes.statement: For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \]
nodes.statement_short: The $L^2$ critical nonlinearity picks up exactly the same conformal prefactor.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Transform the inverse-square potential term
nodes.statement: and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Homogeneity of degree $-2$ makes the potential term scale like the Laplacian.
nodes.section: 3 Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Recombine the terms to recover the equation
nodes.statement: It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Summing the pieces reproduces the original equation evaluated at the transformed arguments.

nodes.name: $|v|$ is also a minimizer
nodes.statement: It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)\le J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer.
nodes.statement_short: Zero energy and minimal mass identify $v$ as a minimizer, hence so is $|v|$.

nodes.name: Positive minimizers are radial
nodes.statement: Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization. Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \intrn \frac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \intrn \frac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert \nabla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla v_0\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert v_0\Vert_{L^2}, \] we get $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0^*)<J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0)$, a contradiction. We deduce that $|v|$ is radial.
nodes.statement_short: Strict improvement under Schwarz symmetrization of the inverse-square term forces radiality.

nodes.name: Identify $|v|$ with a rescaled ground state
nodes.statement: Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad \text{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big(\frac{2}{N}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{H(|v|)^\frac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The radial minimizer $|v|$ is an explicit $L^2$ rescaling of a ground state.

nodes.name: The phase $w=v/|v|$ is constant
nodes.statement:
The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $n$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\inn$. Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $e(\overline{w}
abla w)\equiv 0$, thus \[ |
abla v|^2=|
abla(|v|)|^2+|v|^2|
abla w|^2+2|v|
abla(|v|)\cdot e(\overline{w}
abla w) \] and \[ \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2=\|
abla (|v|)\|_{L^2}^2+\int_{n} |v|^2|
abla w|^2dx. \] Together with Hardy's inequality, this implies that, if $|
abla w|
eq 0$ then $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction. Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: A nonconstant phase would strictly lower the Weinstein functional, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Step 1: Compactness in $L^q(\rn)$
nodes.statement: {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(\rn)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Big\{\frac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\rn} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}=\frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[ \begin{split} \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\le\frac{1}{2}\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) -\frac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\rn}|v_{n_k}|dx \\ &\le\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\le 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (\ref{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\ge 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad \text{and} \quad E(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad\text{and}\quad H(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\rn}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{\rn}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{\rn}|z_k|^{p+1}dx\right)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$. Consequently, by Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(\rn)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset \rn$ such that \begin{equation} \wt{v}_{n_k} \rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\rn), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \wt{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\wt{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(\rn)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\wt{v}_{n_k}\wto v$ weakly in $H^1(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out vanishing and dichotomy by energy contradictions, leaving compactness up to translations.

nodes.name: Step 2: Localization of the translations
nodes.statement:
{\em Step~2: Localization.} We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $n$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|ightarrow\infty$ as $kightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}. We start by showing that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\ge R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(n)$, there exists $C\ge0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\le R^{-2}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\le CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$. Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta. \end{equation*} Note that this inequality will still hold if we increase the value of $R$ or pass to a further subsequence. Let $a>0$ and $ fi\in C_0^\infty([0,\infty))$ be such that $ fi(r)=1$ for $0\le r \le R$, $ fi(r)=0$ for $r\ge R+a$, $0\le fi\le1$ and $\| fi'\|_{L^\infty}\le 1/a$. Then define \[ u_k(x)= fi(|x|) v_{n_k}(x) \quad	ext{and}\quad w_k(x)=(1- fi(|x|))v_{n_k}(x). \] We clearly have $|u_k|,|w_k|\le|v_{n_k}|$, and $\{u_k\},\{w_k\}\subset H^1(n)$ with \[ |
abla u_k|^2 \le 2\left(( fi')^2|v_{n_k}|^2+ fi^2|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \le 2\left(a^{-2}|v_{n_k}|^2+|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \] and \[ |
abla w_k|^2 \le 2\left(( fi')^2|v_{n_k}|^2+(1- fi)^2|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight) \le 2\left(a^{-2}|v_{n_k}|^2+|
abla v_{n_k}|^2ight). \] Furthermore,  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\intrn rac{|u_k|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta, \end{equation*} and \eqref{hardy} yields  egin{equation} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(u_k)=\liminf_{kightarrow\infty} \left(\intrn |
abla u_k|^2dx-c\intrn rac{|u_k|^2}{|x|^2}dxight) \ge (c_*-c)\delta>0. \end{equation} Using the sequences $\{u_k\},\{w_k\}$, we can now rewrite $H(v_{n_k})$ as  egin{align*} H(v_{n_k}) &=H(u_k)+H(w_k) \ &\phantom{=}+\int_{R<|x|<R+a} \Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dx. \end{align*} We will show that there exist $R>0$ as large as we want and $a>0$ such that, up to a further subsequence,  egin{equation} \limsup_{k	o\infty}\left|\int_{R<|x|<R+a} \Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dxight|\le rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{2}. \end{equation} Using \eqref{crucial}, this will imply  egin{equation} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) \ge\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)+ rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{2}>\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k), \end{equation} which will lead to the desired contradiction. To prove \eqref{est0}, we use the above properties of $u_k$ and $w_k$ to observe that  egin{multline} \left|\int_{R<|x|<R+a}\Big[|
abla v_{n_k}|^2-|
abla u_k|^2-|
abla w_k|^2 - rac{c}{|x|^2}\left(|v_{n_k}|^2-|u_k|^2-|w_k|^2ight)\Big]dxight| \ \le 5\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|
abla v_{n_k}|^2dx+4a^{-2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx + rac{3c}{R^2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx. \end{multline} First, by choosing $R>0$ sufficiently large, we will have  egin{equation}  rac{3c}{R^2}\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx \le  rac{3c}{R^2} \|v_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 \le  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{4} \quad	ext{for all} \ k\in\N. \end{equation} The second term in the right-hand side of \eqref{est} is handled using Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$: for any fixed $R,a>0$, we have that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \int_{R<|x|<R+a}|v_{n_k}|^2dx=0. \end{equation} As for the first term, we claim that we can choose $R>0$ as large as we want and $a>0$ such that, up to a subsequence,  egin{equation} 5\int_{R<|x|<R+a}|
abla v_{n_k}|^2dx\le  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{4} \quad	ext{for all} \ k\in\N. \end{equation} Estimates \eqref{term3}--\eqref{term1} prove \eqref{est0}, and hence \eqref{e1}. If the above claim is not true, then using a diagonal argument we can construct a subsequence $\{v_{n_{k_l}}\}$, and a sequence of pairwise disjoint annuli \[ A_j=\{x\inn : R_j<|x|<R_j+a_j\} \quad	ext{with}\quad R_{j+1}>R_j+a_j, \] such that, for all $j\in\{1,\dots,l\}$, \[ \int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx\ge  ar \delta:=  rac{(c_*-c)\delta}{20}>0 \quad	ext{for all} \ n_{k_l}\in\N. \] But then \[ \intrn|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \ge \sum_{j\in\N}\int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \ge \sum_{j=1}^l\int_{A_j}|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx \ge l ar\delta, \] and it follows that \[ \lim_{l	o\infty}\intrn|
abla v_{n_{k_l}}|^2dx=+\infty. \] In view of \eqref{hardy2} this contradicts \eqref{a}, and completes the proof of \eqref{e1}. We will now combine \eqref{e1} with the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN} and the assumption on the energy in \eqref{a} to reach a contradiction. Using Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^{p+1}(n)$. Hence, by \eqref{a},  egin{align*} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})\le rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx = rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx, \end{align*} and so, by \eqref{e1},  egin{align} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)< rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx. \end{align} Using again Step 1 with $|y_k|	o\infty$, we also have that $u_k	o0$ in $L^2(n)$, which implies \[ M_\mathrm{gs}=\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^2} =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\|w_k\|_{L^2}. \] Therefore, \eqref{GN} applied to $w_k$ yields \[  rac{2}{p+1}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx \le\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\left( rac{\|w_k\|_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}ight)^{ rac4N}H(w_k) = \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k), \] which, together with \eqref{e4}, leads to the contradiction \[ \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k)<\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(w_k). \] This shows that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$ and completes the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We now have  egin{align*} \liminf_{k	o\infty} E(v_{n_k}) &=\liminf_{k	o\infty}  rac12 \|
abla v_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 -\lim_{k	o\infty}  rac{1}{p+1} \| v_{n_k}\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}\ &=\liminf_{k	o\infty}  rac12 \|
abla \wt{v}_{n_k}\|_{L^2}^2 -\lim_{k	o\infty}  rac{1}{p+1} \| \wt{v}_{n_k}\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}\ &\ge  rac12 \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2 -  rac{1}{p+1} \|v\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}>E(v)\ge 0, \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from \eqref{posE} with $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. This contradicts \eqref{a} and shows that the sequence $\{y_k\}$ must indeed be bounded in $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Assuming $|y_k|\to\infty$, show the inverse-square term vanishes via a cut-off plus annulus argument, then contradict the energy assumption using Hardy and Gagliardo--Nirenberg.

nodes.name: Step 3: Conclusion
nodes.statement: {\em Step~3: Conclusion.} Suppose, without loss of generality, that $y_k\to y^*\in\rn$. Then \[ v_{n_k}\to v^*=v(\cdot+y^*) \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\rn), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*), \] and $v_{n_k}\wto v^*$ weakly in $H^1(\rn)$. Since the Hardy functional $H$ is weakly lower semi-continuous \cite{montefusco}, and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, it now follows by \eqref{posE} that \[ \begin{split} 0\le E(v^*)=\frac{1}{2}H(v^*)-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\rn}|v^*|^{p+1}dx &\le \frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\rn}|v^*|^{p+1}dx\\ &\phantom{\le}=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})\le 0, \end{split} \] so in fact \begin{equation} E(v^*)=0 \quad\text{and}\quad H(v^*)=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}). \end{equation} Since $\|v^*\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(v^*)=0$, Proposition \ref{charact.prop} yields $v^*=e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}$ for some $\gamma_0\in\real$, $\lambda_0>0$, and some $Q\in \mathcal{G}$. Finally, by \eqref{convergence} and \eqref{hardy2}, we also have that $\|v_{n_k}\|_{H^1}\rightarrow \|v^*\|_{H^1}$. Hence $\{v_{n_k}\}$ converges strongly to $v^*$ in $H^1(\rn)$, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: With bounded translations, weak lower semi-continuity forces $E(v^*)=0$, and the variational characterization identifies the $H^1$ limit as a ground state.

nodes.name: Compute $\Gamma'(t)$
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $\Gamma$ once; the potential and nonlinear terms are real and drop out, leaving the momentum term.
nodes.statement:

Since $u$ satisfies (ef{inls}), we find \[  egin{split} \Gamma'(t)&=2e\int|x|^2 ar{u}\partial_tu=2e\int|x|^2 ar{u}i(\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u)\ &=-2\im\int|x|^2( ar{u}\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}|u|^2+|u|^{p+1})=-2\im\int|x|^2 ar{u}\Delta u. \end{split} \] Integrating by parts and using that $
abla |x|^2=2x$, we obtain \[ \Gamma'(t)=2\im\int

Using again integration by parts, we get \[  egin{split} \Gamma''(t)&=4\im\int\partial_t ar{u}(x\cdot

We use (ef{inls}) to compute the last two terms. We first find  egin{align} -4N\im\int\partial_tu ar{u}&=-4Ne\int ar{u}(\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u)

nodes.statement_short: Summing $A$, $B$, $C$ and the mass term reconstitutes $16E(u)$ plus the nonlinear remainder.

nodes.name: Step 1: Rescaled sequence converges to a ground state
nodes.statement_short: Rescale $u(t_n)$ to unit Hardy functional; the rescaled sequence satisfies the hypotheses of the compactness proposition.
nodes.statement: {\em Step~1.} Let $\{t_n\}_{n\in\nat} \subset \real$ be a sequence of times such that $t_n\uparrow T$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. We set \[ u_n=u(t_n), \quad \lambda_n^2=H(u_n), \quad v_n(x)=\lambda_n^{-N/2}u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x). \] We note that $\lambda_n\rightarrow\infty$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$, and $\|v_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_0\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ by the $L^2$ scaling. Furthermore, \[ \begin{split} H(v_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)=1. \end{split} \] On the other hand, by conservation of the energy, \[ \begin{split} E(v_n)&=\frac12\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)-\frac{1}{p+1}\lambda_n^{-2}\int_{\rn} |u_n(y)|^{p+1}dy\\ &=\lambda_n^{-2} E(u_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}E(u_0)\to 0 \quad \text{as} \ n\to\infty. \end{split} \] Hence, by Proposition \ref{compact.prop}, there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $\gamma_0\in\real$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that, up to a subsequence, \begin{equation} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0, \end{equation} where $Q_{\lambda_0}(x)=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x)$.

nodes.name: Step 2: Mass concentration at the origin
nodes.statement_short: Test against $\varphi\in C_0^\infty$ to show $|u_n|^2\to M_\mathrm{gs}^2\delta_0$ in the sense of distributions.
nodes.statement: {\em Step~2.} We now prove that $u_n$ concentrates all of its mass at $x=0$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. We show that, in the sense of distributions, \[ |u_n|^2\rightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\delta_0. \] Indeed, for any $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(\rn)$, using the change of variables $y=\lambda_n^{-1}x$ we find that \[ \begin{split} \int_{\rn}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy &=\int_{\rn}|u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x)|^2\varphi(\lambda^{-1}_nx)\lambda_n^{-N}dx =\int_{\rn}|v_n(x)|^2\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx\\ &=\int_{\rn}(|v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2)\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx+\int_{\rn} |Q(x)|^2\varphi(0)dx\\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{\rn}|Q(x)|^2(\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0))dx. \end{split} \] Thus, we obtain \[ \begin{split} \Big|\int_{\rn}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy -M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0)\Big| &\le \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty}\int_{\rn}||v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2|dx\\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{\rn}|Q(x)|^2|\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0)|dx. \end{split} \] We conclude this step by noticing that $|v_n|^2$ converges strongly to $|Q|^2$ in $L^1(\rn)$ from (\ref{b}), so the first integral vanishes as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Since $\lambda_n\rightarrow\infty$ the second integral also converges to zero by the dominated convergence theorem. Hence, we obtain \begin{equation} \int_{\rn}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy\rightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Step 3: $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and the exact form of $\Gamma$
nodes.statement_short: Truncated variance plus Banica's inequality give $u(t)\in\Sigma$, and the virial identity then forces $\Gamma(t)=8E(u_0)(T-t)^2$.
nodes.statement:
{\em Step~3.} We now show that $u(t)\in\Sigma$ for all $t\in[0,T)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty_0(n)$ be a radial and non-negative function such that $\phi(x)=|x|^2$ for $|x|\le 1$. It is easy to see that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \[ |
abla \phi (x) |^2\le C\phi(x) \] for all $x\inn$. Indeed, since $\phi$ is radially symmetric we may choose $f\in C(eal,eal_+) $, such that $\phi(|x|)=f(|x|)$. By Taylor's formula, for all $r\ineal$ and $h\ineal$ there exists $y\in[r,r+h]$, such that \[ 0\le f(r+h)=f(r)+f'(r)h+ rac{f''(y)}{2}h^2\le f(r)+f'(r)h+C'h^2, \] where $C'=1+\max_{r\ineal} rac{|f'(r)|}{2}>0$. Since the right-hand side is a positive quadratic polynomial, we must have that $|f'(r)|^2-4C'f(r)\le 0$, thus $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$, where $C=4C'>0$. For all $R>0$, we define $\phi_R(x)=R^2\phi(x/R)$, and for all $t\in[0,T)$, \[ \Gamma_R(t)=\int_{n}\phi_R(x)|u(t,x)|^2dx. \] A direct calculation, similar to the proof of Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, yields that \[ \Gamma_R'(t)=2	ext{Re}\int\phi_R ar{u}\partial_tu =-2	ext{Im}\int\phi_R ar{u}(\Delta u+ rac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u) =2\int
abla\phi_R\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u}
abla u). \] Since $\|u\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$, we can apply Lemma ef{banica.lem} and the inequality $|
abla\phi_R|^2\le C\phi_R$, to get \[ |\Gamma'_R(t)|\le 2\sqrt{2E(u)}\Big(\int|
abla\phi_R|^2|u|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le C\sqrt{E(u_0)}\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}. \] By integrating between a fixed $t\in[0,T)$ and $t_n$, we obtain, \[ |\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}-\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t_n)}|\le C|t-t_n|. \] Applying (ef{c}) in Step 2, we get \[ \Gamma_R(t_n)=\int_{n} |u_n(x)|^2\phi_R(x)dxightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\phi_R(0)=0. \] Thus, letting $n	o\infty$ in the last inequality, we obtain, for all $t\in [0,T)$ and all $R>0$, \[ \Gamma_R(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] Since the right-hand side of the last expression is independent of $R$, letting $R	o\infty$ yields, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)\in\Sigma \quad	ext{and}\quad 0\le \Gamma(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] From this estimate, we can extend by continuity $\Gamma(t)$ at $t=T$ by setting $\Gamma(T)=0$, from which we also obtain $\Gamma'(T)=0$. Moreover, since $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and $u$ is a solution of~\eqref{inls}, we may apply Lemma~ef{virial.lemma}, and by (ef{virialthree}) we obtain $\Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0)$, which finally gives, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ \Gamma(t) = 8E(u_0)(T-t)^2. \] Letting $t=0$, we find, using identity (ef{virialone}) \[ \Gamma(0)=\int |x|^2|u_0|^2= 8E(u_0)T^2 \quad 	ext{and}\quad \Gamma'(0)= 4\int x\cdot\im(\overline{u_0}
abla u_0) = -16E(u_0)T. \]

nodes.name: Step 4: Identification of $u_0$ via the pseudo-conformal transformation
nodes.statement_short: The phase-modulated datum has zero energy and minimal mass, so it is a rescaled ground state; uniqueness then gives $u=S_{\wt Q,T,\tilde\lambda_0,\tilde\gamma_0}$.
nodes.statement: {\em Step 4.} We apply identity \eqref{valeria} with $u_0$, $s=\frac{1}{2T}$, and $\theta(x)=\frac{|x|^2}{2}$ to get \[ \begin{split} E(u_0e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}})&=E(u_0)+\frac{1}{2T}\int x\cdot\text{Im}(\bar{u_0}\nabla u_0) +\frac{1}{8T^2}\int|x|^2|u_0|^2\\ &=E(u_0)+\frac{1}{2T}(-4E(u_0))+\frac{1}{8T^2}(8E(u_0)T^2)=0. \end{split} \] Note that this calculation justifies, {\em a posteriori}, the application of~\eqref{valeria} with $\theta(x)=\frac{|x|^2}{2}\not\in C_0^{\infty}(\rn)$. Since $\|u_0e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}}\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(u_0e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}})=0$, we can deduce from Proposition \ref{charact.prop} that there exist $\lambda_1>0$, $\gamma_1\in\real$, and $\wt{Q}\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ u_0(x)=e^{i\gamma_1}e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}}\lambda_1^{N/2}\wt{Q}(\lambda_1x). \] Finally, we use the pseudo-conformal transformation. We define $\tilde\lambda_0=\lambda_1T>0$ and $\tilde\gamma_0=\gamma_1-\lambda_1^2T\in\real$, and write $u_0$ as \[ u_0(x)=e^{i\tilde\gamma_0}e^{i\frac{\tilde\lambda^2_0}{T}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}}\Big(\frac{\tilde\lambda_0}{T}\Big)^{N/2}\wt{Q}\Big(\frac{\tilde\lambda_0x}{T}\Big). \] Thus, $u_0=S_{\wt{Q},T,\tilde\lambda_0,\tilde\gamma_0}(0)$, where $S_{\wt{Q},T,\tilde\lambda_0,\tilde\gamma_0}$ is defined by (\ref{S2.def}). By invoking uniqueness of the solution of (\ref{inls}), we find that $u(t)=S_{\wt{Q},T,\tilde\lambda_0,\tilde\gamma_0}(t)$ for all $t\in[0,T)$, which concludes the proof.
